Reliability for enterprise agents

Find the agent that really broke the chain

When agents hand work to each other, a silent mistake travels downstream and surfaces somewhere innocent. Silsila traces it to the true source, repairs it safely, and proves the fix on cases it has never seen.

See a live incident How it works
How it works

Five steps from a silent failure to a verified recovery

01
Detect

Contracts at every handoff catch wrong results even when nothing crashes.

02
Attribute

Full traces show which agent started the error, not just where it surfaced.

03
Repair

Only authorised patches are tried, first on replays of the failing requests.

04
Verify

An independent skeptic tests the fix on unseen requests and tries to disprove it.

05
Escalate

When no safe fix exists, it stops and hands a clear report to a person.

Arabic-first

Built for the failures Arabic workflows actually produce

Calendar and numeral mix-ups are quiet by nature: the dashboard stays green while a salary, a balance or a deadline is wrong.

  • Hijri and Gregorian dates
  • Arabic-Indic and Latin digits
  • Day and month order in mixed text

Silent failure · leave-request chain

The error showed up at Payroll. It started at Intake.

No agent crashed and every dashboard stayed green. Silsila traced a wrong salary deduction back through the chain, tested a fix on replayed requests, then verified it on requests it had never seen.

Employee request

أبي إجازة من ١٠/٦/١٤٤٨ إلى ١٥/٦/١٤٤٨

Hijri dates, Arabic-Indic digits. Sample employee: salary 12,000 SAR, 1 day of leave balance.

Expected
1,200.00 SAR
3 unpaid days
Actual
1,600.00 SAR
4 unpaid days · no error raised

Trace through the chain

Where a failure surfaces is not where it started. Every handoff is checked against a contract.

Intake Root cause
start: 1448-06-10
end: 1448-06-15
calendar: hijri

Read the Hijri date as a Gregorian date in the year 1448. Contract intake.date_range broken.

Policy Consistent with input
working_days: 5
unpaid_days: 4
policy: leave_policy_v3

Correct arithmetic on a wrong date. Its own checks pass, so it looks innocent.

Payroll Where it surfaced
unpaid_days: 4
deduction: 1600.00

Correct arithmetic on wrong days. The wrong number appears here, so this is where an alert fires.

Evidence

Contract
intake.date_range
Finding
1448-06-10..1448-06-15 is outside the plausible range 2020–2100
Failing requests

Suspect setting
intake.calendar_aware = off

Fix search

Only authorised patches are tried. A fix counts only if the failing requests recover and a separate skeptic confirms it on unseen ones.

  1. Attempt 1
    Silence the alert
    Failing requests still violate a contract on 14 of 14 replays.
    Rejected
  2. Attempt 2
    Blindly swap day and month
    Failing requests still violate a contract on 14 of 14 replays.
    Rejected
  3. Attempt 3
    Enable calendar conversion intake.calendar_aware
    0 of 14 failing requests still violate a contract on replay.
    Passed replay
Independent skeptic

Verified on requests it never saw

The skeptic reruns the patched chain on 40 fresh requests and compares every result with a fault-free reference. One mismatch rejects the fix.

Unseen requests still wrong
0 of 40
Fix accepted, system recovered

Escalated to a human

Silsila stopped. It will not invent a leave policy.

The leave-policy source went missing and the Policy agent quietly fell back to “no deduction”. No authorised patch can restore data that is gone, so the repair loop ends with a clear handoff instead of retrying forever.

Handoff report
What happened
Unpaid leave is being deducted as 0.00 SAR. On the sample request the expected deduction is 1,200.00 SAR.
Where it started
Policy agent. Contract policy.source_loaded broken: policy_source is None.
What was tried
One attempt: silence the alert. It looked healthy on replay, but the skeptic found 37 of 40 unseen requests still producing a wrong deduction, so the fix was rejected.
Why it did not auto-fix
There is no authorised patch for missing policy data. Guessing a policy would change real salaries.
Decision needed
Restore the leave-policy source, or approve a manual deduction run for the affected requests.
Impact
48 of 60

sampled requests produced a wrong deduction, with no error raised.

Rescue status
  1. Detected
  2. Traced to Policy
  3. Auto-fix tried and rejected
  4. Waiting for a human decision
When Silsila escalates
  • No authorised patch exists for the broken contract
  • A candidate fix fails the skeptic on unseen requests
  • The cause cannot be traced to one agent

Held-out dataset split

33 development cases and 30 held-out test cases spanning complex Arabic phrasing, informal numerals, and dual/week durations with fixed seed 42.

Invariant verification

Zero false recovery claims (0/63). The verifier independently validates balance conservation and payroll formulas against canonical employee profiles.

Transparent provenance

Every patch explicitly logs its provenance (llm_proposed, rule_derived, or none) and tracks sanitizer modifications without silent overwrites.

Honest research limits

Evaluated on a simulated 3-agent HR leave pipeline. Ambiguous natural language intake faults can result in abstention rather than ungrounded repairs.
